# Cineview

> React animation framework centered on scene timelines, with drag and scroll modes. Organize content into Scenes, declare animation durations and dependencies, and advance them through gestures, scrolling, or elapsed time.

These guides target cineview@0.0.1-beta, React 19, and Framer Motion 13. Import `Cineview` with this capitalization. The earlier cineview@1.0.0 uses a different API; do not combine examples from those versions. In a different checkout, confirm package.json and public types before applying these guides.

## Read by task

- [Quick start](docs/ai/quickstart.md): installation, core concepts, a complete drag App, and local development.
- [Timelines](docs/ai/timeline.md): durations, delays, after dependencies, drivers, and timing calculations.
- [Modes](docs/ai/modes.md): drag versus scroll, fixed drag navigation height, scroll zones, and mode-specific parameters.
- [Recipes](docs/ai/recipes.md): complete scroll narrative and video Apps, asset requirements, and expected behavior.

Read quick start first. Add modes when selecting an interaction, timeline when sequencing elements, and recipes for complete implementations. Detailed references can be read only when the task needs them.

## Essential rules

- Each Scene owns its element timeline; there is no page-wide after sequence.
- `timeline.after` references an `animateId` in the same Scene and waits for its entrance to finish, then adds the follower's delay.
- `mode` is `drag` or `scroll`. `timeline.driver` is `scene` or `clock`; a driver is not another page mode.
- Drag navigation stays one viewport high. `Scene.layout.height` sizes inner content only.
- In a scroll zone, 1ms of authored scene-driven duration equals 1px of real scroll distance.
- Use `Scene.scroll={{ zoneId: 'film' }}`. Omit removed fields: root zoneTrigger, Scene.scroll.trigger, Animate.timeline.zoneId, and goToZone align.
- AnimateVideo has its own smaller API; its timeline accepts delay and after, not driver or phase.
- Keep the root dist directory while repository development consumers run. Their dev commands build the linked package before starting Vite.
